title: Choose the look for Beasy
question: The roll assigned the Shade Card direction. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Shade Card
options.lineage: The paint, fabric and tile shade cards every Indian shop counter keeps
options.thesis: Every document is a coded colour chip, so a chat's state reads at a glance like a shade card.
options.viewport: Standard chat list and chat, but each document card wears a solid status chip with its code (INV 0148), and the chat header carries a strip of chips, one per open document.
options.risk: Too many chip colours turn into confetti unless status colours stay strictly reserved.

raised.raise: Turmeric is reserved for 'waiting on you' and appears nowhere else.
Every party owns one chip colour, used on its avatar, its cards and its ledger line.
Every rupee amount and document code is set in one tabular face at real density.
Colour stays flat: no gradients, glass or grain anywhere.
One UI family on a strict type scale; the condensed face appears only on codes.
Pending and the catalog sit on a visible four-column chip grid.

options.label: Bahi-khata
options.lineage: The red cloth-bound ledger of Indian traders
options.thesis: Every chat is a page of the khata, with the running balance always in view.
options.viewport: Chat list where every row ends in the party's running balance in red or green; the chat header is a deep red band with the balance.
options.risk: The most familiar direction for Indian trade, and ruled-ledger backgrounds slide into costume fast.

options.label: Datamatics field
options.thesis: The business as a dense black-and-white data field.
options.case: Loses both axes: shop owners do not see themselves in it, and strobing data hurts a working screen.
options.risk: Cold and hard to read in daylight.
options.kept: Numbers at real density in one tabular face.

options.label: Character catalog
options.thesis: Every customer and supplier as a ranked character.
options.case: Loses both axes: too playful for money and contracts.
options.kept: Each party owns one colour everywhere.

options.label: Design annual plates
options.thesis: Quiet near-white sheets with registration marks.
options.case: Holds clarity but loses audience: it reads as a design studio, not a shop.
options.risk: Too pale for busy daylight use.
options.kept: One type family on a strict scale.

options.label: Grid specimen
options.thesis: A visible construction grid holds everything.
options.viewport: Screens drawn on a visible grid.
options.case: Loses both axes: abstract, no link to how traders work.
options.risk: Reads as a poster, not an app.
options.kept: A visible chip grid for Pending and the catalog.

options.label: Guide map lobes
options.thesis: Areas of the business as swelling colour lobes.
options.case: Loses both axes: a map metaphor hides where things are.
options.risk: Navigation by shapes slows the task.
options.kept: Flat colour with no gradients or texture.

options.label: Orienteering course
options.thesis: Terrain stays fixed while one reserved colour marks the live course.
options.viewport: Pending as a course of numbered controls.
options.case: Loses both axes: few owners know this map language.
options.kept: One colour reserved for what needs you now.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A familiar green-and-white business messenger, executed cleanly.
canonCard.viewport: The chat list and bubbles every WhatsApp Business user already knows.
canonCard.risk: Looks like a WhatsApp clone, which is exactly what Beasy is trying to outgrow.
